01: 1. This Chapter covers all live animals except:
(a) fish and crustaceans, molluscs and other aquatic invertebrates, of heading 0301, 0306, 0307 or 0308;
(b) cultures of micro-organisms and other products of heading 3002; and
02: (a) products of the kinds described in headings 0201 to 0208 or 0210, unfit or unsuitable for human consumption;
(c) guts, bladders or stomachs of animals (heading 0504) or animal blood (heading 0511 or 3002); or
(d) animal fat, other than products of heading 0209 (Chapter 15).
Supplementary Note: In this Chapter, "wild animal" means wild animal as defined in the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972 (53 of 1972).
03: (b) meat of mammals of heading 0106 (heading 0208 or 0210);

(c) fish (including livers, roes and milt thereof) or crustaceans, molluscs or other aquatic invertebrates, dead and unfit or unsuitable for human consumption by reason of either their species or their condition (Chapter 5); flours, meals or pellets of fish or of crustaceans, molluscs or other aquatic invertebrates, unfit for human consumption (heading 2301); or
(d) caviar or caviar substitutes prepared from fish eggs (heading 1604).
2. In this Chapter, the term “pellets” means products which have been agglomerated either directly by compression or by the addition of a small quantity of binder.
3. Headings 0305 to 0308 do not cover flours, meals and pellets, fit for human consumption (heading 0309).
04: 1. The expression "milk" means full cream milk or partially or completely skimmed milk.

2. For the purposes of heading 0403, yogurt may be concentrated or flavoured and may contain added sugar or other sweetening matter, fruit, nuts, cocoa, chocolate, spices, coffee or coffee extracts, plants, parts of plants, cereals or bakers' wares, provided that any added substance is not used for the purpose of replacing, in whole or in part, any milk constituent, and the product retains the essential character of yogurt.

(a) the term "butter" means natural butter, whey butter or recombined butter (fresh, salted or rancid, including canned butter) derived exclusively from milk, with a milkfat content of 80% or more but not more than 95% by weight, a maximum milk solids-not-fat content of 2% by weight and a maximum water content of 16% by weight. Butter does not contain added emulsifiers, but may contain sodium chloride, food colours, neutralising salts and cultures of harmless lactic-acid-producing bacteria;

(b) the expression "dairy spreads" means a spreadable emulsion of the water-in-oil type, containing milkfat as the only fat in the product, with a milkfat content of 39% or more but less than 80% by weight.
4. Products obtained by the concentration of whey and with the addition of milk or milkfat are to be classified as cheese in heading 0406 provided that they have the three following characteristics :
(a) a milkfat content, by weight of the dry matter, of 5% or more;
(b) a dry matter content, by weight, of at least 70% but not exceeding 85%; and
(c) they are moulded or capable of being moulded.
(a) non-living insects, unfit for human consumption (heading 0511);
(b) products obtained from whey, containing by weight more than 95% lactose, expressed as anhydrous lactose, calculated on the dry matter (heading 1702);
(c) products obtained from milk by replacing one or more of its natural constituents (for example, butyric fats) by another substance (for example, oleic fats) (heading 1901 or 2106); or
(d) Albumins (including concentrates of two or more whey proteins, containing by weight more than 80% whey proteins, calculated on the dry matter) (heading 3502) or globulins (heading 3504).

6. For the purposes of heading 0410, the term "insects" means edible non-living insects, whole or in parts, fresh, chilled, frozen, dried, smoked, salted or in brine, as well as flours and meals of insects, fit for human consumption. However, it does not cover edible non-living insects otherwise prepared or preserved (generally Section IV).

1. For the purposes of sub-heading 0404 10, the expression "modified whey" means products consisting of whey constituents, that is, whey from which all or part of the lactose, proteins or minerals have been removed, whey to which natural whey constituents have been added, and products obtained by mixing natural whey constituents.
2. For the purposes of sub-heading 0405 10, the term "butter" does not include dehydrated butter or ghee (sub-heading 0405 90).
Supplementary Note: In this Chapter, "wild animal" means wild animal as defined in the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972 (53 of 1972).
05: (a) edible products (other than guts, bladders and stomachs of animals, whole and pieces thereof, and animal blood, liquid or dried);
(b) hides or skins (including furskins) other than goods of heading 0505 and parings and similar waste of raw hides or skins of heading 0511 (Chapter 41 or 43);
(c) animal textile materials, other than horsehair and horsehair waste (Section XI); or
(d) prepared knots or tufts for broom or brush making (heading 9603).
2. For the purposes of heading 0501, the sorting of hair by length (provided the root ends and tip ends respectively are not arranged together) shall be deemed not to constitute working.
3. Throughout this Schedule, elephant, hippopotamus, walrus, narwhal and wild boar tusks, rhinoceros horns and the teeth of all animals are regarded as "ivory".

4. Throughout the Schedule, the expression "horsehair" means hair of the manes or tails of equine or bovine animals. Heading 0511 covers, inter alia, horsehair and horsehair waste, whether or not put up as a layer with or without supporting material.

Supplementary Note: In this Chapter, the expressions "wild animal" and "wild life" have the meanings respectively assigned to them in clauses (36) and (37) of section 2 of the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972 (53 of 1972); and the expression "wild bird" means any bird specified in Schedules to that Act.
06: 1. Subject to the second part of heading 0601, this Chapter covers only live trees and goods (including seedling vegetables) of a kind commonly supplied by nursery gardeners or florists for planting or for ornamental use; nevertheless it does not include potatoes, onions, shallots, garlic or other products of Chapter 7.

2. Any reference in heading 0603 or 0604 to goods of any kind shall be construed as including a reference to bouquets, floral baskets, wreaths and similar articles made wholly or partly of goods of that kind, account not being taken of accessories of other materials. However, these headings do not include collages or similar decorative plaques of heading 9701.
07: 1. This Chapter does not cover forage products of heading 1214.

2. In headings 0709, 0710, 0711 and 0712, the word "vegetables" includes edible mushrooms, truffles, olives, capers, marrows, pumpkins, aubergines, sweet corn (Zea mays var. saccharata), fruits of the genus Capsicum or of the genus Pimenta, fennel, parsley, chervil, tarragon, cress and sweet marjoram (Majorana hortensis or Origanum majorana).
3. Heading 0712 covers all dried vegetables of the kinds falling in headings 0701 to 0711, other than:
(b) sweet corn in the forms specified in headings 1102 to 1104;
(c) flour, meal, powder, flakes, granules and pellets of potatoes (heading 1105);
(d) flour, meal and powder of the dried leguminous vegetables of heading 0713 (heading 1106).
4. However, dried or crushed or ground fruits of the genus Capsicum or of the genus Pimenta are excluded from this Chapter (heading 0904).

5. Heading 0711 applies to vegetables which have been treated solely to ensure their provisional preservation during transport or storage prior to use (for example, by sulphur dioxide gas, in brine, in sulphur water or in other preservative solutions), provided they remain unsuitable for immediate consumption in that state.

08: 1. This Chapter does not cover inedible nuts or fruits.
2. Chilled fruits and nuts are to be classified in the same headings as the corresponding fresh fruits and nuts.
3. Dried fruit or dried nuts of this Chapter may be partially rehydrated, or treated for the following purposes :
(a) for additional preservation or stabilisation (for example, by moderate heat treatment, sulphuring, the addition of sorbic acid or potassium sorbate);
(b) to improve or maintain their appearance (for example, by the addition of vegetable oil or small quantities of glucose syrup), provided that they retain the character of dried fruit or dried nuts.

4. Heading 0812 applies to fruit and nuts which have been treated solely to ensure their provisional preservation during transport or storage prior to use (for example, by sulphur dioxide gas, in brine, in sulphur water or in other preservative solutions), provided they remain unsuitable for immediate consumption in that state.
09: 1. Mixtures of the products of headings 0904 to 0910 are to be classified as follows :
(a) mixtures of two or more of the products of the same heading are to be classified in that heading;

(b) mixtures of two or more of the products of different headings are to be classified in heading 0910. The addition of other substances to the products of headings 0904 to 0910 [or to the mixtures referred to in paragraph (a) or (b) above] shall not affect their classification provided the resulting mixtures retain the essential character of the goods of those heading. Otherwise such mixtures are not classified in this Chapter; those constituting mixed condiments or mixed seasonings are classified in heading 2103.
2. This Chapter does not cover Cubeb pepper (Piper cubeba) or other products of heading 1211.
(1) Heading 0901 includes coffee in powder form.

(2) "Spice" means a group of vegetable products (including seeds, etc.), rich in essential oils and aromatic principles, and which, because of their characteristic taste, are mainly used as condiments. These products may be whole or in crushed or powdered form.

(3) The addition of other substances to spices shall not affect their inclusion in spices provided the resulting mixtures retain the essential character of spices and spices also include products commonly known as "masalas".

1. Within any one heading of this Chapter, polymers (including copolymers) and chemically modified polymers are to be classified according to the following provisions :
(a) where there is a sub-heading named “Other” in the same series :

(1) the designation in a sub-heading of a polymer by the prefix “poly” (for example, polyethylene and polyamide -6,6) means that the constituent monomer unit or monomer units of the named polymer taken together must contribute 95% or more by weight of the total polymer content;

(2) the copolymers named in sub-headings 3901 30, 3901 40, 3903 20, 3903 30 and 3904 30 are to be classified in those sub-headings, provided that the comonomer units of the named copolymers contribute 95% or more by weight of the total polymer content;
(3) chemically modified polymer are to be classified in the sub-heading named “Other”, provided that the chemically modified polymers are not more specifically covered by another sub-heading;

(4) polymers not meeting (1), (2) or (3) above, are to be classified in the sub-heading, among the remaining sub-headings in the series, covering polymers of that monomer unit which predominates by weight over every other single comonomer unit. For this purpose, constituent monomer units of polymers falling in the same sub-heading shall be taken together. Only the constituent comonomer units of the polymers in the series of sub-headings under consideration are to be compared;
(b) where there is no sub-heading named “Other” in the same series :

(1) polymers are to be classified in the sub-heading covering polymers of that monomer unit which predominates by weight over every other single comonomer unit. For this purpose, constituent monomer units of polymers falling in the same sub-heading shall be taken together. Only the constituent comonomer units of the polymers in the series under consideration are to be compared;

(2) chemically modified polymers are to be classified in the sub-heading appropriate to the unmodified polymer. Polymer blends are to be classified in the same sub-heading as polymers of the same monomer units in the same proportions.

12. For the purposes of headings 8541 and 8542 :

(a) (i) “Semiconductor devices” are semiconductor devices, the operation of which depends on variations in resistivity on the application of an electric field or semiconductor- based transducers. Semiconductor devices may also include assembly of plural elements, whether or not equipped with active and passive device ancillary functions. “Semiconductor-based transducers” are, for the purposes of this definition, semiconductor-based sensors, semiconductor-based actuators, semiconductor- based resonators and semiconductor-based oscillators, which are types of discrete semiconductor-based devices, which perform an intrinsic function, which are able to convert any kind of physical or chemical phenomena or an action into an electrical signal or an electrical signal into any type of physical phenomenon or an action. All the elements in semiconductor-based transducers are indivisibly combined, and may also include necessary materials indivisibly attached, that enable their construction or function. The following expressions mean,—

(1) “Semiconductor-based” means built or manufactured on a semiconductor substrate or made of semiconductor materials, manufactured by semiconductor technology, in which the semiconductor substrate or material plays a critical and unreplaceable role of transducer function and performance, and the operation of which is based on semiconductor properties including physical, electrical, chemical and optical properties.

(2) “Physical or chemical phenomena” relate to phenomena, such as pressure, acoustic waves, acceleration, vibration, movement, orientation, strain, magnetic field strength, electric field strength, light, radioactivity, humidity, flow, chemicals concentration, etc.

(3) “Semiconductor-based sensor” is a type of semiconductor device, which consists of microelectronic or mechanical structures that are created in the mass or on the surface of a semiconductor and that have the function of detecting physical or chemical quantities and converting these into electric signals caused by resulting variations in electric properties or displacement of a mechanical structure.

(4) “Semiconductor-based actuator” is a type of semiconductor device, which consists of microelectronic or mechanical structures that are created in the mass or on the surface of a semiconductor and that have the function of converting electric signals into physical movement.

(5) “Semiconductor-based resonator” is a type of semiconductor device, which consists of microelectronic or mechanical structures that are created in the mass or on the surface of a semiconductor and that have the function of generating a mechanical or electrical oscillation of a predefined frequency that depends on the physical geometry of these structures in response to an external input.

(6) “Semiconductor-based oscillator” is a type of semiconductor device, which consists of microelectronic or mechanical structures that are created in the mass or on the surface of a semiconductor and that have the function of generating a mechanical or electrical oscillation of a predefined frequency that depends on the physical geometry of these structures.

(ii) “Light-emitting diodes (LED)” are semiconductor devices based on semiconductor materials which convert electrical energy into visible, infra-red or ultra-violet rays, whether or not electrically connected among each other and whether or not combined with protective diodes. Lightemitting diodes (LED) of heading 85.41 do not incorporate elements for the purposes of providing power supply or power control;
(b) “Electronic integrated circuits” are :

(i) Monolithic integrated circuits in which the circuit elements (diodes, transistors, resistors, capacitors, inductances, etc.) are created in the mass (essentially) and on the surface of a semi-conductor or compound semi-conductor material (for example, doped silicon, gallium arsenide, silicon germanium, indium phosphide) and are inseparably associated;

(ii) Hybrid integrated circuits in which passive elements (resistors, capacitors, inductances, etc.), obtained by thin- or thick-film technology, and active elements (diodes, transistors, monolithic integrated circuits, etc.), obtained by semi-conductor technology, are combined to all intents and purposes indivisibly, by interconnections or interconnecting cables, on a single insulating substrate (glass, ceramic, etc.). These circuits may also include discrete components;

(iii) Multichip integrated circuits consisting of two or more interconnected monolithic integrated circuits combined to all intents and purposes indivisibly, whether or not on one or more insulating substrates, with or without leadframes, but with no other active or passive circuit elements;

(iv) Multi-component integrated circuits (MCOs) : a combination of one or more monolithic, hybrid, or multi-chip integrated circuits with at least one of the following components : silicon-based sensors, actuators, oscillators, resonators or combinations thereof, or components performing the functions of articles classifiable under heading 8532, 8533, 8541, or inductors classifiable under heading 8504, formed to all intents and purposes indivisibly into a single body like an integrated circuit, as a component of a kind used for assembly onto a printed circuit board (PCB) or other carrier, through the connecting of pins, leads, balls, lands, bumps, or pads. For the purpose of this definition:
(1) “Components” may be discrete, manufactured independently then assembled onto the rest of the MCO, or integrated into other components.
(2) “Silicon based” means built on a silicon substrate, or made of silicon materials, or manufactured onto integrated circuit die.

(3) (a) “Silicon-based sensors” consist of microelectronic or mechanical structures that are created in the mass or on the surface of a semiconductor and that have the function of detecting physical or chemical phenomena and transducing these into electric signals, caused by resulting variations in electric properties or displacement of a mechanical structure. “Physical or chemical phenomena” relates to phenomena, such as pressure, acoustic waves, acceleration, vibration, movement, orientation, strain, magnetic field strength, electric field strength, light, radioactivity, humidity, flow, chemicals concentration, etc.

(b) “Silicon based actuators” consist of microelectronic and mechanical structures that are created in the mass or on the surface of a semi- conductor and that have the function of converting electrical signals into physical movement.

(c) “Silicon based resonators” are components that consist of microelec- tronic or mechanical structures that are created in the mass or on the sur- face of a semi-conductor and have the function of generating a mechani- cal or electrical oscillation of a predefined frequency that depends on the physical geometry of these structures in response to an external input.

(d) “Silicon based oscillators” are active components that consist of microelectronic or mechanical structures that are created in the mass or on the surface of a semi-conductor and that have the function of generating a mechanical or electrical oscillation of a predefined frequency that depends on the physical geometry of these structures. For the classification of the articles defined in this Note, headings 8541 and 8542 shall take precedence over any other heading in this Schedule, except in the case of heading 8523, which might cover them by reference to, in particular, their function.

1. In this Section and, where applicable, throughout this Schedule, the following expressions have the meanings hereby assigned to them :
(a) Unbleached Yarn Yarn which:
(i) has the natural colour of its constituent fibres and has not been bleached, dyed (whether or not in the mass) or printed; or

(ii) is of indeterminate colour ("grey yarn"), manufactured from garnetted stock. Such yarn may have been treated with a colourless dressing or fugitive dye (which disappears after simple washing with soap) and, in the case of man-made fibres, treated in the mass with delustring agents (for example, titanium dioxide).
(b) Bleached Yarn Yarn which:
(i) has undergone a bleaching process, is made of bleached fibres or, unless the context otherwise requires, has been dyed white (whether or not in the mass) or treated with a white dressing;
(ii) consists of a mixture of unbleached and bleached fibres; or
(iii) is multiple (folded) or cabled and consists of unbleached and bleached yarns.
(c) Coloured (dyed or printed) Yarn Yarn which:
(i) is dyed (whether or not in the mass) other than white or in a fugitive colour, or printed, or made from dyed or printed fibres;

(ii) consists of a mixture of dyed fibres of different colours or of a mixture of unbleached or bleached fibres with coloured fibres (marl or mixture yarns), or is printed in one or more colours at intervals to give the impression of dots;
(iii) is obtained from silvers or rovings which have been printed; or

(iv) is multiple (folded) or cabled and consists of unbleached or bleached yarn and coloured yarn. The above definitions also apply, mutatis mutandis, to monofilament and to strip or the like of Chapter 54.
(d) Unbleached Woven Fabric Woven fabric made from unbleached yarn and which has not been bleached, dyed or printed. Such fabric may have been treated with a colourless dressing or a fugitive dye.
(e) Bleached Woven Fabric Woven fabric which:
(i) has been bleached or, unless the context otherwise requires, dyed white or treated with a white dressing, in the piece;
(ii) consists of bleached yarn; or
(iii) consists of unbleached and bleached yarn.
(f) Dyed Woven Fabric Woven fabric which:

(i) is dyed a single uniform colour other than white (unless the context otherwise requires) or has been treated with a coloured finish other than white (unless the context otherwise requires), in the piece; or
(ii) consists of coloured yarn of a single uniform colour.
(g) Woven Fabric of Yarns of Different Colours Woven fabric (other than printed woven fabric) which :
(i) consists of yarns of different colours or yarns of different shades of the same colour (other than the natural colour of the constituent fibres);
(ii) consists of unbleached or bleached yarn and coloured yarn; or
(iii) consists of marl or mixture yarns. (In all cases, the yarn used in selvedges and piece ends is not taken into consideration).

(h) Printed Woven Fabric Woven fabric which has been printed in the piece, whether or not made from yarns of different colours. (The following are also regarded as printed woven fabrics : Woven fabrics bearing designs made, for example, with a brush or spray gun, by means of transfer paper, by flocking or by the batik process). The process of mercerisation does not affect the classification of yarns or fabrics within the above categories. The definitions at (d) to (h) above apply, mutatis mutandis, to knitted or crocheted fabrics.

(i) Plain Weave A fabric construction in which each yarn of the weft passes alternately over and under successive yarns of the warp and each yarn of the warp passes alternatively over and under successive yarns of the weft.

1.65% or more of manganese -
0.08% or more of molybdenum -

2. Subject to Note 1 to this Section, Note 1 to Chapter 84 and to Note 1 to Chapter 85, parts of machines (not being parts of the articles of heading 8484, 8544, 8546 or 8547) are to be classified according to the following:

(a) Parts which are goods included in any of the headings of Chapter 84 or 85 (other than headings 8409, 8431, 8448, 8466, 8473, 8487, 8503, 8522, 8529, 8538 and 8548) are in all cases to be classified in their respective headings;

(b) Other parts, if suitable for use solely or principally with a particular kind of machine, or with a number of machines of the same heading (including a machine of heading 8479 or 8543) are to be classified with the machines of that kind or in heading 8409, 8431, 8448, 8466, 8473, 8503, 8522, 8529 or 8538 as appropriate. However, parts which are equally suitable for use principally with the goods of headings 8517 and 8525 to 8528 are to be classified in heading 8517;
(c) All other parts are to be classified in heading 8409, 8431, 8448, 8466, 8473, 8503, 8522, 8529 or 8538 as appropriate or, failing that, in heading 8487 or 8548.

3. Unless the context otherwise requires, composite machines consisting of two or more machines fitted together to form a whole and other machines designed for the purpose of performing two or more complementary or alternative functions are to be classified as if consisting only of that component or as being that machine which performs the principal function.

4. Where a machine (including a combination of machines) consists of individual components (whether separate or interconnected by piping, by transmission devices, by electric cables or by other devices) intended to contribute together to a clearly defined function covered by one of the headings in Chapter 84 or Chapter 85, then the whole falls to be classified in the heading appropriate to that function.
5. For the purposes of these Notes, the expression "machine" means any machine, machinery, plant, equipment, apparatus or appliance cited in the headings of Chapter 84 or 85.
XVII: 1. This Section does not cover articles of heading 9503 or 9508 bobsleighs, toboggans and the like of heading 9506.
2. The expressions "parts" and "parts and accessories" do not apply to the following articles, whether or not they are identifiable as for the goods of this Section:
(a) Joints, washers or the like of any material (classified according to their constituent material or in heading 8484) or other articles of vulcanised rubber other than hard rubber (heading 4016);
(b) Parts of general use, as defined in Note 2 to Section XV, of base metal (Section XV), or similar goods of plastics (Chapter 39);
(c) Articles of Chapter 82 (tools);
(d) Articles of heading 8306;

(e) Machines and apparatus of headings 8401 to 8479, or parts thereof, other than the radiators for the articles of this Section, articles of heading 8481 or 8482 or, provided they constitute integral parts of engines and motors, articles of heading 8483
(f) Electrical machinery or equipment (Chapter 85);
(a) Articles of Chapter 90;
(b) Articles of Chapter 91;
(ij) Arms (Chapter 93);
(k) Lamps or lighting fittings of heading 9405; or
(l) Brushes of a kind used as parts of vehicles (heading 9603).

3. References in Chapters 86 to 88 to "parts" or "accessories" do not apply to parts or accessories which are not suitable for use solely or principally with the articles of those Chapters. A part or accessory which answers to a description in two or more of the headings of those Chapters is to be classified under that heading which corresponds to the principal use of that part of accessory.
4. For the purposes of this Section:
(a) Vehicles specially constructed to travel on both road and rail are classified under the appropriate heading of Chapter 87;
(b) Amphibious motor vehicles are classified under the appropriate heading of Chapter 87;
(c) Aircraft specially constructed so that they can also be used as road vehicles are classified under the appropriate heading of Chapter 88.
5. Air-cushion vehicles are to be classified within this Section with the vehicles to which they are most akin as follows:
a) In Chapter 86 if designed to travel on a guide-track (hovertrains);
b) In Chapter 87 if designed to travel over land or over both land and water;
c) In Chapter 89 if designed to travel over water, whether or not able to land on beaches or landing - stages or also able to travel over ice.
Parts and accessories of air-cushion vehicles are to be classified in the same way as those of vehicles of the heading in which the air-cushion vehicles are classified under the above provisions.

Hovertrain track fixtures and fittings are to be classified as railway track fixtures and fittings, and signalling, safety or traffic control equipment for hovertrain transport systems as signalling, safety, or traffic control equipment for railways.

disputes.note: A solar photovoltaic module/panel is 8541 43 00 (photovoltaic cells assembled in modules or made up into panels) — not 8501 (electric generators) and not 8504. A complete 'solar power generating system' put up together may be classified as a system; the bare module is 8541. GST rate for solar cells/modules and many renewable-energy devices is a concessional slab — confirm the current rate entry.
Solar water heaters and systems are 8419 12 00 (solar water heaters), not 8516 (electric water heaters). GST: solar water heater and system attract a concessional rate — check the entry.

The distinction: an LED *light source* (the lamp/bulb/tube itself, i.e. the replaceable module) is 8539 (electric filament or discharge lamps, incl. LED lamps 8539 52). A complete LED *luminaire / fitting* (panel light, downlight, streetlight, fixture with driver and housing) is 9405. Bare LED chips/modules for assembly can be 8541. All commonly 18%.

Flavoured milk is a 'beverage containing milk' of 2202 99 — not 0402 (milk and cream) — because flavouring takes it out of Chapter 4. Confirmed by CBIC Circular 52/26/2018 and AAR rulings. The tariff item was 2202 99 30 until 30 April 2026 and is 2202 99 31 / 2202 99 39 from 1 May 2026 (01/2026-CTR); see the rate finder for the rate in force.

Plain chapati / roti (ready to eat) is 1905, Nil/5%. Frozen/packaged parathas that need further cooking were held by AAR (and upheld) to be 2106 (food preparations n.e.s.) at 18% — different from roti because they are not 'ready to eat' and contain more than flour and water. Widely litigated; check the latest position.

Ready-to-eat / ready-to-cook preparations (idli mix, gulab jamun mix, dosa mix, instant upma, packaged curries) are generally 2106 90 (food preparations n.e.s.), 18% — unless the product is squarely a preparation of a specific heading (e.g. pasta 1902, a soup 2104). The addition of ingredients beyond a single cereal flour usually pushes it to 2106.

Alcohol-based hand sanitiser is a disinfectant of 3808 94 00 (CBIC Circular / Board clarification during COVID), 18% — not 3004 (medicament) and not 3401/3402 (soap/washing preparation). A non-alcoholic antiseptic in measured doses could be 3004; the ordinary retail sanitiser is 3808.

Car seat covers and car floor mats made for a specific vehicle model are parts/accessories of motor vehicles → 8708, 28%/18%. Generic textile covers or mats not identifiable to a vehicle stay in the textile / plastics heading. The 'suitable for use solely or principally' test (Section XVII Note 3) decides.

'Parts of general use' — bolts, nuts, screws, springs (7320), chains (7315), tubes, and similar articles of base metal — are ALWAYS classified in their own heading (Section XV Note 2), never as a part of the machine or vehicle they fit. A bolt for a car engine is 7318, not 8708/8409.

Printers, copiers and multifunction print/scan/copy machines are 8443 (8443 31 for machines that connect to an ADP machine/network; 8443 32 other). Since HS 2007 they are NOT in 8471 (ADP machines) even though they attach to a computer. 18%.

A monitor 'of a kind solely or principally used in an ADP system' is 8528 52 (still Chapter 85, not 8471). A monitor that can also receive a TV signal, or a large display, is 8528 59 / 8528 72. Both are commonly 18%. The reception capability and the 'principally used with ADP' test decide the sub-heading.

A smartwatch with cellular / data communication is 8517 (reception/transmission apparatus), 18% — not Chapter 91 (watches). A simple activity band with no communication function and a time display may fall in 9102. The communication function is decisive (GRI 3(b) essential character).
A power bank is an accumulator (it contains lithium-ion cells) → 8507 60 00, 18% — not 8504 (static converter / charger). CBIC has clarified this. A bare charger/adaptor with no cells is 8504 40.

A set-top box for gaining access to internet / receiving TV, not incorporating a display, is 8528 71, 18%. Not 8517 (even though it may have network functions) — the reception-for-television character governs.

A CCTV / IP surveillance camera is a television camera of 8525 83 / 8525 89, 18% — not 9006 (photographic still cameras) and not 8517. If sold as a full CCTV *system* (cameras + DVR + cables), classify by GRI 3(b) — usually still 8525 unless the recorder dominates (8521).

An e-rickshaw for carrying passengers is a motor vehicle of 8703 (specifically the electric-vehicle sub-heading), 5% under the EV concession — not 8711 (motorcycles) and not 8704 unless it is a goods carrier. The number of wheels and passenger-carrying design govern.

A hybrid motor car is still 8703 — the sub-heading (8703 40 / 8703 60 for petrol-electric, 8703 50 / 8703 70 for diesel-electric, vs 8703 21-24 for pure IC) and engine capacity decide the rate and cess. It is NOT 8703 80 (that is 'only electric motor'). Get the powertrain description exactly right.

An on-road tipper / dumper for transporting goods is 8704 (motor vehicles for the transport of goods). A dumper 'designed for off-highway use' is 8704 10 (a distinct sub-heading). A dumper that is really construction machinery (e.g. an articulated site dumper) may be 8429/8430. The road-use test matters for both rate and cess.
The trailer/trolley towed behind a tractor is 8716 (trailers and semi-trailers), 18% — separate from the tractor itself (8701, 5%). Do not classify the trolley with the tractor.

The battery is an electric accumulator of 8507 (8507 20 lead-acid tubular, 8507 60 lithium-ion), 18-28% depending on type — classified separately from the inverter/UPS (8504) it powers, even when sold together, unless genuinely put up as a set (then GRI 3(b)).

Parts of mobile phones — display assemblies, batteries (also 8507), chargers (also 8504), PCBAs — have specific GST entries. The Government has notified many mobile parts at a specific rate; a phone battery is 8507, a charger 8504, a display/PCBA 8517 70. Do not default everything to 8517.

Parts of railway locomotives and rolling stock are 8607 — but 'parts of general use' (bolts, springs) are excluded to Section XV, and articles that are goods of another heading (bearings 8482, seats 9401) go there. Section XVII Notes 2 and 3 apply.

Artificial flowers, foliage and fruit are 6702 (6702 10 of plastics, 6702 90 of other materials), 18% — not Chapter 39 (plastics) and not 9505 (festive articles), because 6702 is the specific heading. A garland assembled from them is still 6702.

disputes.heading: any
disputes.note: A rakhi is a 'puja samagri' item — CBIC clarified (Circular 52/26/2018) that a rakhi other than one that is a form of imitation jewellery is exempt (Nil). A rakhi that is essentially imitation jewellery is 7117. Kalava / sacred thread is Nil.
Sanitary towels/napkins and tampons are 9619; sanitary napkins are Nil-rated under GST. A menstrual cup is also Nil. Do not classify in Chapter 39/40/56.

Footwear is classified by outer-sole material then upper material (Chapter 64) — 6401 waterproof, 6402 rubber/plastics, 6403 leather upper, 6404 textile upper, 6405 other. GST rate turns on SALE VALUE: footwear of sale value not exceeding Rs 1,000 per pair is 12%, above is 18% (confirm the current threshold and slab).

Garments are classified by knitted (Ch 61) vs woven (Ch 62), then by garment type and fibre. GST rate turns on SALE VALUE: an article of apparel of sale value not exceeding Rs 1,000 per piece is 5%, above is 18% (confirm the current threshold).

Woven fabric is classified by chief-weight fibre (Section XI Note 2) — cotton (52), man-made filament (54), man-made staple (55), then by weight per m2 and weave. 'Chief weight' means the single textile material that predominates by weight; blends are decided against every other material together.

A composite supply of goods + services for immovable property (construction, fabrication, erection, fitting out, renovation) is a WORKS CONTRACT SERVICE under SAC 9954, taxed as a service — not as a supply of the goods. Rate depends on the nature (residential / commercial / government / EPC) — check Notification 11/2017-CTR entry.

disputes.heading: any
disputes.note: A machine that performs two or more complementary functions is classified as if it consisted only of that component / performed only that function which is the PRINCIPAL function (Section XVI Note 3). If no single function is principal, GRI 3(c) — last heading in numerical order.

disputes.heading: any
disputes.note: Goods put up in a set for retail sale that cannot be classified to one heading are classified by the component that gives the set its ESSENTIAL CHARACTER (GRI 3(b)). If a set is really several separately-priced items sold together, each is classified on its own. There is no HSN for 'gift set'.

disputes.heading: any
disputes.note: A PART is integral — the machine cannot function without it. An ACCESSORY adds a function or convenience but the machine works without it. For Section XVI/XVII, both a part and an accessory 'suitable for use solely or principally with' a machine follow that machine — but only if the part/accessory is not itself a good of another heading and is not a part of general use.

A charger / adaptor / SMPS / LED driver is a static converter of 8504 40, 18% — it converts AC to DC or changes voltage. It is not a part of the appliance it powers (unless built in). A power bank (with cells) is 8507, not 8504.

A kitchen chimney / range hood is 8414 60 00 (hoods having a maximum horizontal side not exceeding 120 cm), 18% — it is a fan/ventilation article of 8414, not a kitchen appliance of 8509 and not 8516.

A domestic water purifier (RO / UV / UF) is filtering or purifying machinery for liquids → 8421 21, 18% — not 8509 (domestic appliances) and not 8479. Replacement filter cartridges are 8421 99 (parts).

Imitation jewellery (no precious metal, or only plating) is 7117, 3% under GST. Bangles of lac / glass may be 7018 / 7117 depending on construction. Real gold/silver jewellery is 7113. Watch out: a rakhi that is imitation jewellery is 7117, not exempt.

Statuettes and ornaments of wood, wood marquetry, jewellery/cutlery caskets of wood are 4420. Many handicrafts have specific concessional GST entries (handmade / traditional craft). Identify the material and the article; 'handicraft' is not itself a classifier.

Disposable tableware of paper/paperboard is 4823; of plastics is 3924; of areca leaf / bagasse / moulded pulp is 4823 (or the plant-material heading). GST rate differs by material and there are concessions for compostable / areca products — check the entry.

Preparations of a kind used in animal feeding — compound feed, feed supplements, mineral mixtures for cattle — are 2309, Nil under GST. A pure vitamin or a pure mineral chemical is its own Chapter 29/28 heading. Pet food put up for retail is 2309 10 (taxable).

disputes.heading: any
disputes.note: Two units of the SAME product taped together is not a 'set' — it is just that product. A pack of DIFFERENT products (shampoo + conditioner) put up for retail is a set → GRI 3(b), classified by essential character.

Parts of air-conditioning machines are 8415 90. But a compressor presented separately is 8414 30 (compressors of a kind used in refrigerating equipment), the refrigerant gas is Chapter 29/38, and 'parts of general use' go to Section XV. An indoor/outdoor unit of a split AC is still 8415.

Ceramic sinks, wash basins, WC pans, cisterns, bidets and similar sanitary fixtures are 6910, 18% — not 6815 (articles of stone) and not 3922 (of plastics) unless the article is actually of that material. 'Sanitary ware' in trade means the ceramic fixture.

0402.covers: Milk and cream, concentrated or containing added sugar/sweetener — milk powder, condensed milk, dairy whitener.
0402.excludes: Flavoured milk (2202 99 — flavouring leaves Chapter 4); ghee (0405); infant formula put up for retail (1901 10).
0402.test: Concentration or added sugar, with nothing added that takes it out of Chapter 4.

0406.covers: Cheese and curd of all kinds — paneer/chena, processed cheese, mozzarella, cottage cheese.
0406.excludes: Products where non-dairy ingredients dominate; whey (0404).
0406.test: Pre-packaged and labelled paneer is Nil under GST 2.0; unlabelled loose paneer is also Nil.

1905.covers: Bread, pastry, cakes, biscuits, rusks, communion wafers, empty cachets, pizza (not stuffed), khakhra, plain chapati/roti, papad.
1905.excludes: Frozen parathas needing further cooking (held to be 2106); stuffed pasta (1902); namkeen/bhujia (2106).
1905.test: A baked or dried product of flour dough, ready to eat. If it needs cooking and has ingredients beyond flour+water+fat, look at 2106.

2106.covers: Food preparations not elsewhere specified — instant mixes (idli/dosa/gulab jamun), ready-to-cook curries, namkeen/bhujia/mixture, protein/nutrition powders, sugar syrups, supari/betel-nut preparations, pan masala.
2106.excludes: A preparation that is squarely a good of a specific heading — pasta (1902), soup (2104), sauce (2103), chocolate (1806), ice cream (2105).
2106.test: 'Not elsewhere specified' — only reach 2106 after checking the specific food headings. Pan masala 2106 90 20 attracts 28% + compensation cess.

2202.covers: Waters with added sugar or flavour, aerated waters, and 'other non-alcoholic beverages' — flavoured milk, fruit-juice-based drinks, energy drinks, soya/plant milk drinks.
2202.excludes: Fruit/vegetable juice of 2009 (unfermented, no added spirit — but added sugar is allowed there); mineral water with nothing added (2201).
2202.test: Under GST 2.0 caffeinated beverages, carbonated beverages with fruit juice and plain aerated waters are 40% (Schedule III of 09/2025-CTR); fruit-pulp / fruit-juice drinks that are not carbonated, and beverages containing milk (flavoured milk), are 5% (Schedule I) — see the rate finder for the codes.

3004.covers: Medicaments — mixed or unmixed products for therapeutic or prophylactic use, put up in measured doses or in retail packing. Includes Ayurvedic/Siddha/Unani/Homoeopathic medicaments (3004 90).
3004.excludes: Food supplements / nutraceuticals not for the treatment of a disease (2106 or 2202); disinfectants and sanitisers (3808); medicated soap (3401).
3004.test: A therapeutic/prophylactic purpose against a specific ailment, in measured doses or retail packs. Marketing as a 'health supplement' points away from 3004.

3808.covers: Insecticides, rodenticides, fungicides, herbicides, disinfectants and similar products put up for retail sale — mosquito repellents, phenyl-type disinfectants, alcohol-based hand sanitiser.
3808.excludes: A cleaning preparation whose function is washing, not disinfecting (3402); a medicament for treating infection in a person (3004).
3808.test: The product's declared function is to kill or repel pests / micro-organisms.

4202.covers: Trunks, suitcases, vanity cases, briefcases, school satchels, handbags, wallets, spectacle cases, camera cases, tool bags, sports bags, jewellery boxes — the 'containers' heading.
4202.excludes: A fitted case presented with the article it holds and giving the whole no essential character (goes with the article, GRI 5(a)); crates and industrial packing (Chapter 39/44/73).
4202.test: Outer surface material decides the sub-heading — leather, plastic sheeting, textile, vulcanised fibre, paperboard.

4823.covers: Other articles of paper/paperboard — paper trays, plates, cups, cut-to-size paper, gaskets of paper, moulded/pressed articles of paper pulp, paper bobbins.
4823.excludes: Cartons and boxes (4819); printed matter (Chapter 49); decorative laminates (often 4823 — check construction).
4823.test: An article of paper/paperboard not covered by a more specific heading (4816-4822).

6109.covers: T-shirts, singlets, vests — knitted or crocheted.
6109.excludes: Woven T-shirt-like garments (6208/6211); knitted shirts with a collar and full-length opening (6105/6106).
6109.test: Knitted or crocheted construction. GST rate turns on sale value (Rs 1,000/piece threshold).

6403.covers: Footwear with outer soles of rubber/plastics/leather/composition leather and uppers of LEATHER.
6403.excludes: Uppers of textile material (6404); all-rubber or all-plastic footwear (6402); sports footwear with spikes may still be 6403/6404.
6403.test: Outer sole material, then upper material. GST rate turns on sale value (Rs 1,000/pair threshold — confirm current slab).

7113.covers: Articles of jewellery and parts thereof, of precious metal or of metal clad with precious metal — gold/silver chains, rings, bangles, mangalsutra, necklaces, studded jewellery.
7113.excludes: Imitation jewellery with no precious metal (7117); coins (7118); precious-metal articles that are not jewellery (7114 goldsmiths' wares).
7113.test: Contains precious metal (even as cladding). GST 3% on jewellery; making charges separately 5%.

7117.covers: Imitation jewellery — of base metal (plated or not), of plastics, oxidised, kundan/CZ costume jewellery, hair ornaments other than of 9615.
7117.excludes: Any jewellery containing precious metal (7113); glass bangles (7018); articles that are really something else (a keychain 8308).
7117.test: No precious metal at all. GST 3%. A rakhi that is essentially imitation jewellery is 7117, not exempt.

7318.covers: Screws, bolts, nuts, coach screws, screw hooks, rivets, cotters, washers, and similar articles of iron or steel — a 'part of general use' (Section XV Note 2).
7318.excludes: Nothing by end-use — a bolt for an aircraft is still 7318, never 8803.
7318.test: If it is a threaded or non-threaded fastener of base metal, it is here regardless of what it fastens.

8207.covers: Interchangeable tools for hand tools or machine-tools — drill bits, taps, dies, milling cutters, threading tools, press tools, rock-drilling bits.
8207.excludes: The powered tool itself (8467 hand, 8457-8465 machine); hand tools worked by hand (8201-8205).
8207.test: An interchangeable working part that is fitted to a tool or machine, whether hand- or power-operated.

8415.covers: Air-conditioning machines with a motor-driven fan and elements for changing temperature and humidity — window, split, cassette, ductable, packaged AC; car AC (8415 20).
8415.excludes: An evaporative air cooler (8479 60); a refrigerator (8418); a fan alone (8414); a dehumidifier (8479).
8415.test: Combines a fan + a refrigeration/heating element in one machine. Parts of AC are 8415 90; a bare compressor is 8414 30.

8418.covers: Refrigerators, freezers, refrigerating/freezing equipment, heat pumps (other than AC of 8415) — domestic fridges, deep freezers, water coolers, visi-coolers, ice-cream freezers.
8418.excludes: Air conditioners (8415); a simple ice box with no refrigerating unit.
8418.test: Contains a refrigerating unit (compressor/absorption). Combined refrigerator-freezers with separate external doors are 8418 10.

8443.covers: Printing machinery; and printers, copiers and facsimile machines (8443 31/32), whether or not combined, including those that connect to an ADP machine or network.
8443.excludes: 8471 (ADP machines) — since HS 2007 printers are NOT ADP units even though they attach to a computer.
8443.test: A machine that prints, copies or faxes. Ink/toner cartridges are 8443 99 (parts) or Chapter 32/96 depending on type.

8471.covers: Automatic data processing machines and units thereof — laptops, desktops, servers, tablets that meet Chapter 84 Note 6; keyboards, mice, and other input/output units 'of a kind solely or principally used' with an ADP machine; storage units.
8471.excludes: Smartphones and communication-first devices (8517); monitors (8528); printers (8443); a machine performing a specific function with an ADP machine built in (classified by its function, Note 6(E)).
8471.test: Chapter 84 Note 6 — freely programmable, runs a stored program the user can change, of a kind used in an ADP system.

8517.covers: Telephone sets including smartphones; base stations; machines for reception/conversion/transmission of voice/images/data — routers, modems, switches, network cards; smartwatches with communication; video phones.
8517.excludes: ADP machines (8471); TV reception apparatus (8528); radio broadcast receivers (8527).
8517.test: The principal function is communication over a wired or wireless network. Parts of mobile phones have their own notified GST entries.

8528.covers: Monitors and projectors not incorporating TV reception apparatus (8528 42/52/62 — incl. ADP monitors); and TV reception apparatus of all kinds (8528 71 without display, 8528 72 colour, 8528 73 monochrome).
8528.excludes: 8471 (a monitor is Chapter 85, never 8471); video recording/reproducing apparatus (8521).
8528.test: Reception capability (TV tuner) and whether it is principally used with an ADP machine decide the sub-heading. Common rate 18%.

8703.covers: Motor cars and other motor vehicles principally designed to carry PERSONS — sedans, hatchbacks, SUVs, station wagons, racing cars; also three-wheeled passenger vehicles and vehicles for the disabled if motorised.
8703.excludes: Goods vehicles (8704); vehicles for 10+ persons including driver (8702); tractors (8701); motorcycles (8711).
8703.test: Sub-heading by engine type (spark/compression/electric/hybrid) and, for IC engines, cylinder capacity and length. Rate + compensation cess vary widely — get the powertrain and dimensions exact.

8708.covers: Parts and accessories of motor vehicles of 8701-8705 — bumpers, brakes, gearboxes, axles, road wheels, silencers, radiators, clutches, steering, suspension, body parts, seat belts, and model-specific seat covers/mats.
8708.excludes: Parts of general use (Section XV — bolts 7318, springs 7320); goods of another heading (engines 8407/8408, bearings 8482, batteries 8507, lighting 8512, glass 7007, seats 9401); tyres (4011).
8708.test: Section XVII Note 3 — 'suitable for use solely or principally with' vehicles of 8701-8705, and not excluded by Note 2.

8714.covers: Parts and accessories of motorcycles and bicycles (8711-8713) — frames, forks, brakes, saddles, pedals, gear systems, bicycle chains (8714 99 10), wheels.
8714.excludes: Parts of general use; bearings (8482); lighting (8512); goods of another heading.
8714.test: Solely or principally for a cycle or motorcycle.

9018.covers: Instruments and appliances used in medical, surgical, dental or veterinary sciences — syringes, needles, catheters, BP monitors, ECG, ultrasound, dental drills, endoscopes, diagnostic apparatus.
9018.excludes: General-purpose instruments not specially for medical use; spectacles (9004); hearing aids (9021); wheelchairs (8713); disinfectants (3808).
9018.test: Designed for a medical/surgical/dental/veterinary purpose. Many devices attract a concessional GST rate — check the entry.

9021.covers: Orthopaedic appliances, splints, fracture appliances, artificial parts of the body, hearing aids, pacemakers, crutches, surgical belts, intra-ocular lenses.
9021.excludes: Wheelchairs (8713); general medical instruments (9018); spectacles for vision correction (9004).
9021.test: Compensates for a defect or disability, or replaces a body part. Hearing aids and many assistive devices are concessionally rated or Nil.

9403.covers: Other furniture (not seats of 9401, not medical of 9402) and parts — tables, desks, cupboards, wardrobes, almirahs, bookcases, filing cabinets, kitchen/bedroom/office furniture, of any material.
9403.excludes: Seats (9401); mattresses and bedding (9404); lamps (9405); prefab buildings (9406); goods of Chapter 94 Note 1 exclusions (e.g. plastic hinges, safes 8303).
9403.test: A movable article designed to be placed on the floor/ground to equip a home/office/shop. Sub-heading by material. Almost all 18%.

9405.covers: Luminaires and lighting fittings — chandeliers, ceiling/wall lights, table/desk/floor lamps, LED panel lights and downlights, streetlights, floodlights, illuminated signs, decorative lighting sets; and parts.
9405.excludes: The LED lamp / bulb / tube itself as a light source (8539); portable torches with own power source (8513); vehicle lighting (8512).
9405.test: A complete fitting that holds and positions a light source. The replaceable lamp inside is 8539.

9503.covers: Tricycles, scooters, pedal cars, dolls' carriages, dolls, other toys, reduced-size models, and puzzles of all kinds — including toys combined with an incidental non-toy item (Chapter 95 Note 4) put up for retail with the essential character of a toy.
9503.excludes: Articles identifiable as intended exclusively for animals (classified in their own heading, e.g. pet toys); video game consoles (9504); sports equipment (9506); real bicycles (8712).
9503.test: Designed for the amusement of children or adults. GST — toys are generally 12%, but 'electronic toys' were carved to 18% (9503 00 91).

9506.covers: Articles and equipment for general physical exercise, gymnastics, athletics, other sports (including table-tennis) or outdoor games — cricket bats/balls, footballs, badminton rackets, gym equipment, treadmills, yoga mats, swimming gear.
9506.excludes: Toys (9503); sports footwear (Chapter 64); sports clothing (Chapter 61/62); playing cards (9504); requisites for billiards, casino and automatic bowling (9504).
9506.test: Genuine sports/exercise use rather than amusement.

9619.covers: Sanitary towels (pads) and tampons, napkins and napkin liners for babies (diapers), and similar articles, of any material.
9619.excludes: Absorbent cotton wool (3005); wadding of textile (5601); articles of apparel.
9619.test: An absorbent hygiene article. Sanitary napkins/pads are Nil-rated; baby and adult diapers are taxable.
